pr_title: crypto: make crypto.sign() support poly1305 mac
pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/32433

@nodejs/crypto this needs input on design decisions.

1. What should the "create raw private key" API look like?

2. Is `crypto.sign()` the right place?

`crypto.createSign()` doesn't feel right because you need to provide the key upfront rather than at `sign.sign()` time.

You also can't just substitute `EVP_DigestInit_ex()` with `EVP_DigestSignInit()`.

`crypto.createHmac()` doesn't feel right either because poly1305 is a MAC, not a HMAC.
pr_comments: What about reusing existing properties inside the object that'd be passed to `createPrivateKey()`? So in the case of poly1305, a plain object is passed in whose `key` property would still contain the (binary/raw) key data but the `type` property would be set to `'poly1305'` and `format` would then be ignored.
@mscdex I followed your suggestion and I added support for siphash as a way of demonstrating the extensibility of that approach.
Isn't the key a shared `'secret'` between sender and receiver, and not a `'public'`/`'private'` key pair? (Referring to the `KeyObject.type` property.)

@tniessen It is a 'key', however it's implemented this way because of the underlying OpenSSL API. We could write our own "MAC" API for `crypto` *now* that encompasses HMAC, Poly1305, SIPHash, etc., but with the current OpenSSL releases I feel like the code would end up being less straight forwarding internally because of the different considerations needed for different algorithms.

Once [`EVP_MAC`](https://www.openssl.org/docs/manmaster/man3/EVP_MAC.html) is available, things will be a lot easier implementation-wise since we could just have a node API that more or less passes values on to OpenSSL as-is and supplying the required values would be on the user. Until then, I see the changes in this PR as a temporary measure to allow access to these specialty algorithms.

> The reason it's private instead of secret is that `crypto.sign()` currently only accepts private keys.

@bnoordhuis That's fair, but as you said, poly1305 is also not really a signing algorithm.

bnoordhuis/io.js@fcda409512 is what `crypto.createMac()` would look like. Pretty interchangeable with `crypto.createHmac()` to no one's surprise.

I'll open a draft PR for easier review.

This PR likely became stale after the upgrade to openssl 3 and it definitely has conflicts so I'm going to close it out. EVP_MAC  is available now so that's probably what we want to be pursuing instead?

issue_context.title: crypto: poly1305 message authentication code
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I can't use poly1305 separately from chacha20-poly1305. Some algorithms (e.g. chacha20-poly1305 in OpenSSH) require the operations to be separate due to limitations/restrictions of chacha20-poly1305 as defined in RFC 7539.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
To be able to use poly1305 as efficiently as possible, whether it's via `crypto.createHmac()` or `crypto.sign()` or something else.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Unfortunately there are none, except doing poly1305 in pure javascript, which I assume is going to be pretty slow in comparison.
comments: Supposedly it's already [supported via the EVP_PKEY API](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/2128), so maybe it just requires some minor changes on the node side?

Ah, your mention of `crypto.createHmac()` threw me off.

`crypto.sign(null, data, privateKeyObject)` in theory supports poly1305 out of the box but there's currently no way to construct an `EVP_PKEY` that's acceptable to `EVP_DigestSignInit()`.

We'd need to slot in a call to `EVP_PKEY_new_raw_private_key(EVP_PKEY_POLY1305, key, len)` somewhere but I'm not sure where.

I'll open a conversation starter PR.

There has been no activity on this feature request for 5 months and it is unlikely to be implemented. It will be closed 6 months after the last non-automated comment.

For more information on how the project manages feature requests, please consult the [feature request management document](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/HEAD/doc/contributing/feature-request-management.md).
@mscdex is this still someone you want to see? I have an old open PR but updating it is probably quite a bit of work.
Yes it is still something I'd like to see. Right now I'm having to use a WASM-based implementation, which I'm not really fond of for various reasons.

I closed the PR and I'll take the liberty of closing this issue because it's about poly1305 only, whereas exposing EVP_MAC is a more general way forward.

If you're interested in that, can you open a new issue to hash out<sup>1</sup> the details?

<sup>1</sup> mac out?

review_comments: I initially wrote something like what you suggest but then I noticed similar code a few lines up and decided to go with that for consistency.

Sigh. Yeah, there's quite a bit of inconsistency in the code base for this case. `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` uses different logic for generating the message string for when reporting directly on the argument or a property on the argument. In this case, since it is `key.key` that is being tested, `key.key` should be used in the error message and the other similar cases likely should be fixed.
